bluf: Resoneo is an independent search specialist consultancy with a French language site and no headquarters, founding year or office in the record; it sells SEO first, then GEO, paid search and shopping, and analytics, and claims more than 90 expert consultants. The record shows no dated move, no news, no jobs and no named client; its one visible push is a LinkedIn ad selling Shopping CSS to French ecommerce merchants. Where it points is AI: GEO for ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity and an 'AI Inside' nav item. A rival should know almost nothing about its book is public and its own house tests could not be run.
doing:
The positioning line, an independent search engine specialist covering SEO, GEO, paid search and shopping, data and media performance so brands show up on every search channel, decodes to one promise: presence wherever a query is typed or asked, sold by specialists rather than a full service shop. The headline claim is headcount: more than 90 expert consultants. The nav adds certifications and awards, press coverage, tools and R&D, white papers and a '20 ans ensemble' (20 years together) section, none captured in detail.

The sold mix, breadth 9, has one lead line: SEO at score 3, its first expertise, spanning technical, semantic, netlinking and local work. Core at score 2: AI Search / GEO (the homepage opens on being present in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and AI Overviews), Paid Search (a Search & Shopping expertise run by SEA consultants; the homepage cites Performance Max and AI Max) and Data & Measurement (data strategies named as a specialism). Paid Social, Programmatic & CTV, Local and Content & Digital PR score 1 with no evidence note. The service list also carries international management and training. The only proprietary item is AI Inside, a nav label whose details were not captured; no partners are listed.

AI posture: it pitches AI applied to search as an expertise and sells GEO for visibility in LLMs; the record shows no AI product, tool or case behind the label.

Moves: the record lists none, and no news; the deepen pass found 0 open roles and no ATS. The latest dates are 2 case study archive pages, Search & Shopping on 27 August 2025 and SEO on 22 September 2025, whose excerpts are menu text rather than cases.

Pricing: none in the record. Conspicuously absent for a firm claiming 90+ consultants: a headquarters, offices, a founding year, a named client, a dated case and a publishing record the compile could measure.
clients:
Client type: mixed, on the ICP read; the record lists no verticals and no home market. The market is inferred: the case archives are titled in French, and the one LinkedIn ad, opening 'Depuis juillet 2018', says the leading French ecommerce merchants have used CSS services to pay for Google Shopping clicks since July 2018. French online retailers are therefore the likeliest buyers of its Search & Shopping line (moderate confidence), and the international management line suggests clients running search in several countries (low confidence).

Named clients: none. The needs read names no client, 0 observed and 0 names only, so no need code carries a signal and nothing is shared with another tracked agency's book. The deepen pass counted 2 case study pages, both archive indexes; the white papers and press coverage in the nav were not captured. The silence is a finding: a rival cannot see whom it serves, and neither can a prospect comparing agencies.

What the base likely needs next is inferred from the sold mix. Under KJ1 (The click is being replaced by the citation) it is likely its SEO clients ask for presence in AI answers, which its GEO line sells without an audited scorecard. Under KJ2 (ads inside AI answers) there is a roughly even chance its Shopping and Performance Max buyers ask to test ads in assistants, a move it shows no sign of making. Under KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out) it is likely, low confidence, that the SEO and paid search hours they buy come under price pressure.

openings:
The strongest opening is proof. The record names no client, dates no case and could not test its house, while it sells SEO and GEO on a headcount claim. It is likely, moderate confidence, that a rival bringing named, dated search and AI visibility results into French retail and ecommerce pitches beats it on evidence. Falsifier: dated case studies naming clients, or a client list, on its site at the next compile.

Second, AI visibility: it sells GEO with no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial) and no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent); a rival with a citation share scorecard and an entity service likely leads with both. Third, its paid search and Shopping line shows no sign of testing ads inside assistants (P8 absent): the first agency in its segment to show results there sets the price. Fourth, KJ6 exposure on SEO and paid search hours plus no public pricing make a transparent, outcome priced offer the natural undercut (likely, low confidence). The computed idle sitemap opening is weak, because the read was incomplete.
